scope.current_boundary: Teach angular speed and use omega = 2pi / T and v = r omega. Do not teach centripetal force or centripetal acceleration.
scope.previous_boundary_used: The radian and expressing angular displacement in radians. This lesson recalls only that one revolution is 2pi radians.
scope.next_boundary_checked: A perpendicular force and centripetal acceleration. These are deliberately not taught here.

question_patterns_used.name: Direct calculation
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Two original worked examples show formula choice, units and the linked angular and linear speed route.

question_patterns_used.name: Explanation
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: The lesson distinguishes angular and linear speed and repairs radius, diameter and formula-choice misconceptions.

questions_visited.why_selected: Direct mapped angular-speed calculation in circular motion.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Select and use an angular-speed relationship after an earlier speed result.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Relate circular-path speed and radius to angular speed.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using diameter instead of radius, or treating linear and angular speed as the same quantity.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped evidence uses omega and period, although the opened part is an alternating-current context.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Determine a period from a sinusoidal expression.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Interpret omega and period through omega = 2pi / T.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Confusing angular speed with frequency or omitting 2pi.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped period calculation, opened to check the stated period demand.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify period as the time for one complete cycle before calculation.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating a partial cycle or a length as if it were the period.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped evidence includes a graph-derived period, although the opened part is an oscillation context.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Read a period from a graph and use it later.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Read a complete-cycle time before substitution.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Reading a peak to the next zero rather than between matching points.

questions_visited.why_selected: Immediate predecessor evidence, opened to keep radian treatment as recall only.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Recall the geometry of an arc equal to the radius.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Calling a radian a distance rather than an angle.

questions_visited.why_selected: Second current radian recall item, opened to confirm prerequisite scope.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Recall the angle subtended by an arc equal to the radius.
